text:
Ingrid - Acme Integrations: Hey support, embedding endpoint is returning vectors length 512 but our client unpacks expecting 768 and then throws a reshape error. Happening intermittently when we switch to batching. Example response attached. Can someone help?

Lee - Support: Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste the exact request body you send when it fails? Also which model/endpoint are you calling?

Ingrid - Acme Integrations: Sure — here's the curl we've been using (we tried a few variants, same issue):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"embed-default-large","input":[["Payment reconciliation row: id=1234, amount=42.00"]] }'

And server returns 200 with embedding array length 512: 
{ 
  "object": "embedding",
  "embedding": [0.0012, 0.0023, ...],
  "vector_length": 512
}

In our Java client we then do: reshape(embedding, [768]) and it fails. This only started when we switched to client batching that wraps single items as nested arrays.

Lee - Support: Thanks. Two quick things: 1) confirm the model id you expect to get 768 from (embed-default-large?), 2) it looks like your payload uses input as nested array [ ["text"] ] which sometimes causes the server to treat the inner array as precomputed embedding or a single-vector payload. Could be a normalization edge.

Sam M - ML Eng: jumping in — models vary: some embedding models we surface return 512 (smaller models), others 768+ (base/large). But the payload shape can cause different codepaths. If the server sees an array of numbers it treats it as "you posted an embedding" vs an array of strings => request for text -> encode. Nested arrays like [["x"]] are ambiguous: is it a batch-of-batches or a single item that happens to be a list? We should accept both shapes, but current validation is brittle.

Darren - Backend Eng: I looked at the request traces for Ingrid's org. The router logs show the request body exactly as sent (input: nested list). Our pre-validator runs a quick heuristic: if the first element of the first array is a number -> assume embedding given; if it's a string -> treat as text. But when nested lists exist, we unwrap only one level; when the client wrapped again (batcher returns [["..." ]] ), our unwrap step mis-indexed and we ended up feeding an empty string into the encoding fallback, which selected the smaller 512-dim model variant for performance. That's why the vector_length is 512.

Lee - Support: Can you paste the exact server log snippet (request body + selected model) for the failing request? Customer would prefer a short ETA for a fix or workaround.

Darren - Backend Eng: log snippet: 

[router] req_id=abc123 body={"model":"embed-default-large","input":[["Payment reconciliation row: id=1234, amount=42.00"]]}
[validator] unwrapped_input=["Payment reconciliation row: id=1234, amount=42.00"] (ok)
[model_select] chosen_model=embed-default-small (512 dims) 
[invocation] output_len=512

So the validator appears to have unwrapped correctly in this trace, but an adjacent codepath (batch coalescer) accidentally used the nested list as a pre-batched input and chose the small model for throughput.

Sam M - ML Eng: That matches a race in the batching switch that I filed last quarter — if the batcher sees a nested list it treats it as pre-batched and tries to be 'helpful' by using a faster small embedding model. We should not change model selection based purely on shape.

Lee - Support: For now can Ingrid try sending the request with a single-level list (one of these forms) to confirm workaround?

Correct single-item forms that should be accepted by the API: 
1) Single string as input (no batch): {"model":"embed-default-large","input":"Payment reconciliation row..."}
2) Single-element list (batch of 1): {"model":"embed-default-large","input":["Payment reconciliation row..."]}
NOT nested list: {"model":"embed-default-large","input":[["Payment reconciliation row..."]] } // avoid this

Ingrid - Acme Integrations: OK switching to input as ["..."] fixed it immediately — we now get vector_length=768. Thanks. But our client-side batcher library does double-wrap when batch size=1. It's a pretty common pattern (it returns a list-of-batches).

Ingrid - Acme Integrations: Follow up: can Redwood make the API accept nested single-element lists? It's a common source of confusion. Also would be great to get a clearer error when dimensional mismatch happens (currently we return vector but the client only sees later reshape error).

Sam M - ML Eng: Agreed. Action items: 1) make validator normalize payload shapes (unwrap nested single-element lists automatically), 2) do not use payload shape as a model-size heuristic, 3) improve error message for dimension mismatch when client expects a shape incompatible with returned vector.

Darren - Backend Eng: I'm on it. Plan: small patch to the validator that runs a 'normalize_input' step — unwrap single-element nested lists until reaching a primitive (string or number) or until a safe depth (3). Also add a guard that prevents model selection from looking at shape alone. I'll open PR and include unit tests. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Lee - Support: Great. I'll reply to Ingrid with the workaround and ETA. Also adding a doc snippet under "embeddings -> payload shapes" to call out the three acceptable forms and show the common bad-case.

Ingrid - Acme Integrations: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Small ask: can we get a temporary note in the API response when we detect double-wrapped input? e.g., a warning field so our SDK can detect and auto-normalize before reshaping.

Darren - Backend Eng: We can add a lightweight "warnings" array in the response for a hotfix (no behavior change). I'll include a conditional: if we auto-unwrap, add a warning: "input was nested and was auto-normalized". That should avoid breaking clients.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: "normalize-embeddings-payload" to staging at 2026-03-15T22:40:00Z

Sam M - ML Eng: Also adding a quick unit test for client SDKs in devex to ensure both single-string, single-list, and nested-single-list are normalized. Lee, can you ask the customer to share the name of the batcher lib they use so devex can add an example?

Lee - Support: Will do. Ingrid, can you DM the client library name/version? 

Ingrid - Acme Integrations: Sent DM — it's our in-house batcher but modeled off of a popular open-source lib. We'll try to update on our side too. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Darren - Backend Eng: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/4523 - implementing normalize_input + warnings. Rolling to staging now.

Lee - Support: Marking this thread resolved for customer follow-up. Please post here when prod deploy is complete so I can close the ticket.

Darren - Backend Eng: Prod deploy scheduled tomorrow morning after soak. I'll post the prod completion message in this thread.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: "normalize-embeddings-payload" to production at 2026-03-16T07:05:12Z

Darren - Backend Eng: Prod deploy done. We added: - automatic unwrap of nested single-element lists (depth <=3) - response.warnings array when auto-normalization occurred - removed model-selection heuristics based on payload shape.

Lee - Support: Ingrid, you should be unblocked. If you still see a mismatch after today's deploy please reopen ticket.

Ingrid - Acme Integrations: Verified — nested case now returns 768 and we see response.warnings: ["input was nested and auto-normalized"]. All good. Thanks for the quick fix!

Lee - Support: Closing thread. Notes: update docs, add SDK snippet, and add a regression test in our CI to prevent reintroduction.

Darren - Backend Eng: Added regression tests and linked them in the PR.

Sam M - ML Eng: Added a short note in the release changelog about the warnings field.

Lee - Support: :white_check_mark: Done.
